newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Telecom to invest S$16mln by March.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Telecom to invest S$16mln by March.

text.p: Telephone company Singapore Telecommunications Ltd will have invested a total of Singapore $16 million in infrastructure to support its expanding Internet service by the end of March next year, the company said on Monday.
Telecom internet unit SingNet has seen its customer base grow 12-fold in the last 18 months, Telecom said in a statement.
When internet access was introduced in July 1994, the company started with a modest investment of S$1.2 million and a system which could support 50 users on-line at any one time.

SingNet has been improving its international connections by setting up direct links with countries such as Australia, Hong Kong, Japan and Malaysia, which allow for intra-Asian traffic to be routed within Asia without having to cross the Pacific.
The company said that from Monday SingNet will offer a roaming service called SINGNET Global service.
This would enable subscribers to log in while they are in nine destinations -- U.S., Japan, Hong Kong, Brunei, the Phillipines, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia and Malaysia.
Users will pay a traffic charge of 10 cents per minute plus a log in charge of 50 cents each time they sign on.
